title: Colloquy
text:
I had died for Beauty;

silence and solitude enclosed me,

when they laid near my grave

someone who died for Truth.


In the gentle colloquy we began,

neighbors in the gloomy estate,

he told me and I understood: We are brothers;

Beauty and Truth are one.


And so, beneath the night, behind the stone,

our transparent brotherhood conversed

until ivy covered our faces

and eternity erased our names.
editorial_note: The translation follows the Spanish Dickinson version and keeps the grave-dialogue between Beauty and Truth.

title: A Bird Advances in My Garden...
text:
A bird advances in my garden

on a wheel with spokes-

of persistent music,

like a wandering mill-


it never lingers

on the ripe rose-

it samples without settling,

praises as it departs,


when it has tasted every flavor-

its magical cabriolet

goes whirling into distances-

then I draw near my dog,


and the two of us wonder

whether our vision was real-

or whether we had dreamed the garden

and those curiosities-


but he, being more logical,

points out to my clumsy eyes-

the vibrating flowers!

Subtle answer!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the hummingbird-like motion as wheel, music, and proof in trembling flowers.

title: Safe in Their Alabaster Chambers...
text:
Safe in their alabaster chambers,

insensible to dawn and noon,

the meek members of resurrection sleep,

satin beam and roof of stone.


Light laughs at the breeze in its castle above them,

the bee murmurs in an undisturbed ear;

sweet birds trill in unheeded cadence,

ah, how much wisdom perished here!


Solemnly the years pass, swelling, over them;

worlds gather their arches and firmaments row,

diadems are thrown down and doges surrender,

silent as dots on a disk of snow.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the Spanish version's alabaster tombs and cosmic empires falling silently.

title: A Word Seeks My Wakefulness...
text:
A word

        seeks my wakefulness,

as pure as dawned weeping,

as young as a

        hunted deer,

as deep, flower of flowers, as the sky.


A graceful salve whose flight

may celebrate, unharmed May, your surrendered

        calm; an unforgetting word

that on its knees may name your consolation.


A burning bird, a ballad,

a fragrant song, a harmony

        being born like your saving breeze.


As pure as your gaze is clean!

As young as your joy is born!

        As deep as the creating soul!
editorial_note: The translation keeps Azcoaga's search for a word pure, young, and deep enough for consolation.
